policy: Every source item is accounted for. already-applied means the current manuscript contains the requested qualification; phase16-verified-no-change means the later citation gate closed the provenance concern without a prose edit; escalated means scientific source checking remains necessary and no new fact was inferred.

resolutions.note: The manuscript distinguishes the 26% feasibility ceiling from the 25% and 11% replication-success audits.
Scarcity is limited to robust cross-model validation and the growing tool set is acknowledged.
The higher support for specific high-benefit scenarios is stated as a counter-facet.
Checklist efficacy is qualified by the randomized null result and enforcement context.
The later high-risk citation verification found no actionable correction; the audit trail is retained in Phase 16 artifacts.
The 2.4/10 and 2–3/10 values require full-text confirmation; figure caveats are retained and no new attribution is asserted.
The 80% value is explicitly attributed to one analyst as an illustration.
The donor-motivation discussion is explicitly identified as outside the animal-data scope.
The >120-confounder clause is attributed only to Yap2022.
Mone2020 is attached to NAM-enhanced read-across and excluded from the FDA Modernization Acts clause.
The promissory clause uses Kopanska2022; Marx2025 appears with the adoption-reality discussion.
The DILI performance values are explicitly presented as reported by a qualification review.
The 65–86% and 36–74% carcinogenicity values require confirmation against the Karmaus2026 full text.
The image-duplication baseline is explicitly described as an earlier systematic screen cited secondarily by Richardson2025.
The specialty audit is framed as an additional specialty within a wider multi-field pattern.
Automated whole-literature improvement is contrasted with item-level manual audits.
The 20-of-27 result is attributed only to Pavlovic2025.
The manuscript identifies the psychology/ecology-to-animal transfer and the smaller animal-specific evidence.
